ADR-017：站內搜尋的後續技術路線
所屬專案：Kestrel（自建全文搜尋引擎，2025 Q4 啟動）
決策日期：2026-06-02　決策者：CTO 王志豪、架構委員會（5 票同意、1 票棄權）

背景
Kestrel 的目標是用 Rust 自建倒排索引與排序服務，取代現行的 MySQL LIKE 查詢，原訂 2026/07/31 交付 v1，支援商品、文章、店家三種索引。截至 5 月底，索引建置與基本查詢已能運作，但中文斷詞、同義詞、拼寫校正與相關性調校都還沒開始，團隊估計至少還要兩季。
同一期間，資料平台組完成了託管 OpenSearch 的評估：在 3,000 萬筆商品資料上 p95 查詢延遲 85ms，中文分析器與同義詞功能現成可用，每月費用約 NT$18 萬。

考慮過的選項
1. 繼續 Kestrel，並增聘 2 名搜尋工程師：成本最高，而且年底前仍達不到商用品質。
2. Kestrel 縮小範圍，只做商品索引：大約 9 月可交付，但維運負擔仍全在我們身上。
3. 停止 Kestrel，改用託管 OpenSearch。

決策
採用選項 3。Kestrel 自 6/2 起終止，不再開發，原定的 v1 搜尋服務不會交付，repo 轉為唯讀封存。站內搜尋改由新成立的「OpenSearch 導入」專案負責，該專案由資料平台組主導，另訂時程與預算。

後果
- 正面：每季省下約 4 人月的開發與維運人力；搜尋品質可望在第三季改善。
- 負面：既有的 Rust 索引程式碼與基準測試工具不再維護；對託管服務商產生依賴，合約中須寫入資料匯出條款。
- 人員：Kestrel 的三位工程師，兩位轉入 OpenSearch 導入專案，一位回推薦系統組。
- 硬體：兩台 64 核索引主機於 6/20 前歸還機房，改撥給 log 平台。

附記
架構委員會同場也討論了推薦系統的 feature store 選型（ADR-018，下次會議再決議），以及 API gateway 的升級時程，兩者與本 ADR 無關。

ADR-042：Halcyon 資料湖倉的儲存擴充方案
所屬專案：Halcyon（企業資料湖倉，2026 Q2 啟動，原訂 2027/02/28 完成第一階段）
提出人：資料架構師 Vincent Tsai　日期：2026-12-01

背景
Halcyon 第一階段要把 14 個業務系統的資料以 Iceberg 格式匯入物件儲存，並提供 Trino 查詢。目前 6 個系統的 ingestion pipeline 已在測試叢集上正常運作；剩下 8 個系統（包含資料量最大的 POS 與 CRM）需要把儲存擴充到正式環境的 1.2PB 規模。本 ADR 比較三種擴充方案：
A. 地端新增 12 台 storage 節點（約 NT$1,900 萬）
B. 改用公有雲物件儲存（每月約 NT$62 萬）
C. 混合：熱資料放地端、冷資料上雲

評估摘要
五年 TCO 以 C 案最低，但維運複雜度最高；B 案最快，約 3 週可就緒；A 案要等設備交期，約 10 週。

決議與現況
本 ADR 原訂在 11/27 的架構委員會表決。11/26 財務長發出通知：2027 年度預算重新審查期間，Halcyon 的所有新支出一律凍結，包含採購與雲端合約，要等 1 月中旬董事會的預算審查完成後，再決定是否繼續投資。因此三個方案目前都無法執行；沒有正式環境的儲存，剩下 8 個系統的 ingestion 無法往下做，已完成的 6 個 pipeline 維持在測試叢集，不做任何擴充。本 ADR 改列 Deferred，預算結論出來後再重新提案。

後果
- 測試叢集上 6 個 pipeline 已匯入的資料，先保留到 2027 年 3 月底。
- 外包的 2 位資料工程師合約 12/31 到期，不續約。
- 各業務單位的報表需求，仍由舊資料倉儲支應。

相關事項
- 舊資料倉儲（Teradata）的維護合約已延長到 2027 年底。
- 「行銷 CDP」專案原本預計共用 Halcyon 的資料，該案 10 月已由行銷處自行取消，與本 ADR 無關。

ADR-009：Quill 協作編輯器的同步引擎更換
所屬專案：Quill（企業內部文件協作編輯器）　決策狀態：Accepted　日期：2026-08-14
參與者：前端架構 Aaron、後端 Betty、PM 林家瑜、SRE Chris

背景
Quill 原訂 9/1 對全公司開放 Beta，核心功能是多人同時編輯同一份文件，目前以 Yjs 作為 CRDT 同步引擎。7 月底的壓力測試發現兩個問題：(1) 50 人以上同時編輯一份長文件時，瀏覽器記憶體會漲到 2GB 以上；(2) 我們自行實作的離線合併在表格結構上會產生重複列，已有 14 個重現案例，社群也有人回報同樣問題，但還沒有修正。

考慮的選項
1. 繼續用 Yjs，自行修補表格合併：Aaron 評估修補要深入內部資料結構，風險高，未來升級也困難。
2. 改用 Automerge 2.x：記憶體表現較好，表格以 list-of-maps 表示可以避免重複列，但 API 差異大，編輯器綁定層要重寫。
3. 改成以伺服器為中心的 OT（operational transform）：要重寫後端並放棄離線編輯，不符需求。

決策
採用選項 2，以 Automerge 取代 Yjs。

後果
- 編輯器綁定層與離線儲存要重寫，Aaron 估計 3 週；Betty 的後端同步服務也要調整約 1 週，可以並行。
- Beta 開放日由 9/1 改為 9/22，林家瑜已在 8/15 通知各部門的試用窗口。重寫已經開工，第一版綁定層預計 8/28 進入內部測試。
- 舊的 Yjs 文件格式需要轉換工具，由 Betty 負責，Beta 前完成。
- Beta 的功能範圍不變，仍包含表格、留言與版本紀錄。

附註
- 與本 ADR 無關：設計系統組的「Icon 元件庫 3.0」已取消，Quill 繼續沿用 2.x 版圖示。
- 下次架構會議將討論 Quill 的權限模型是否改接 Okta 群組。

背景
Beacon 要在購物中心 7 層樓提供 3 公尺以內的室內定位，用於 App 導航與店家推播。軟體部分（地圖編輯器、App 定位 SDK 介面、後台）已依兩種技術都能套用的抽象層完成，剩下的工作全都取決於訊號技術：硬體採購、場域佈建、韌體與定位演算法。

選項比較
1. BLE beacon：單價約 NT$450，電池 2 年，定位誤差 3–5 公尺，iOS／Android 原生支援。

ADR-031：Vega 推薦引擎的 feature store 選型
所屬專案：Vega（電商首頁個人化推薦，預定 2026/04/15 全站上線）
作者：ML 平台 Grace Chen　日期：2026-03-03　決策狀態：Accepted

背景
Vega 目前的線上特徵由 Spark 批次計算後寫入 Redis，離線訓練用的特徵另存在 Hive，兩邊的程式邏輯分開維護，已出過 3 次 training-serving skew，導致上線版本的推薦點擊率比離線評估低 8%。我們需要一個 feature store 來統一特徵定義。

選項
1. Feast（開源）：與現有 Redis／Hive 相容，需自行維運。
2. 雲端廠商的託管 feature store：功能完整，但資料要搬到該雲，資料治理審查至少 6 週。
3. 維持現狀，只加強測試：無法根治 skew。

決策
採用 Feast，部署在現有的 Kubernetes 叢集，線上儲存沿用 Redis，離線儲存沿用 Hive。

時程影響評估
Feast 的 POC 已在 2/24–3/2 完成，40 個核心特徵遷入後，skew 測試全數通過。剩下 85 個特徵的遷移，ML 平台組估計要 2 週，預計 3/20 完成，正好銜接 3/23 開始的全站 A/B 測試；4/15 全站上線的日期不需變動，中間還有一週緩衝。託管方案光治理審查就要 6 週，選它就趕不上，這也是沒有選它的原因之一。

後果
- ML 平台組負責 Feast 的升級與監控，SRE 同意納入 on-call。

ADR-007：Orchid 會員點數上鏈方案的去留
所屬專案：Orchid（以聯盟鏈發行跨品牌會員點數，2026/03 啟動）
撰寫：架構師 Dennis 葉　決策會議：2026-10-19 產品暨架構聯席會議　決策狀態：Accepted

背景
Orchid 的目標，是讓集團旗下 5 個品牌的會員點數以聯盟鏈（Hyperledger Fabric）記帳，點數可以跨品牌互換，並開放外部合作商家加入，原訂 2027/01 上線第一階段。截至 9 月，鏈上記帳與 3 個品牌的錢包整合已完成，測試環境的交易吞吐達 800 TPS。

觸發事件
9 月主管機關發布新的函釋：可跨品牌、跨商家流通，且能兌換現金等值商品的點數，認定為類似儲值支付工具，發行者須申請電子支付執照並提撥履約保證。法遵處評估，集團申請執照至少要 18 個月，履約保證需凍結約 NT$3 億。

選項
1. 取得電子支付執照後再上線：時程與資金成本都無法接受。
2. 縮小為單一品牌內使用：失去跨品牌互換的核心價值，而且單一品牌的點數系統早已存在，不需要區塊鏈。
3. 終止 Orchid。

決策
聯席會議 10/19 採用選項 3：Orchid 終止，不再開發，第一階段不上線，跨品牌點數互換的構想一併撤回。鏈上測試網路 11 月底關閉，測試資料依資安規範銷毀。

後果
- 錢包整合程式中的會員身分驗證模組，可以移植到集團的統一會員中心，由會員中心團隊評估。
- Fabric 節點的雲端資源於 11/30 前釋放，每月約省 NT$26 萬。
- Orchid 團隊 6 人中，4 人轉到統一會員中心專案，2 人轉到資料平台。

附註
本次聯席會議也核准了「統一會員中心 2.0」的預算；該案是獨立專案，時程不受本 ADR 影響。

ADR-031: Replace the nightly batch reconciliation with streaming reconciliation for Ledgerline (the general-ledger rebuild for Altamira Freight). Status of this record: accepted. Author: Wen Zhao. Last updated 2 June 2026.

Context
Ledgerline replaces the twenty-year-old COBOL general ledger with a set of services on Postgres. The program charter, signed in January, commits to cutting over the accounts-payable and accounts-receivable books on June 30, 2026, the end of the fiscal half-year. The finance controller chose that date so the new system starts on a clean period boundary.

The current design reconciles sub-ledgers against the general ledger in a nightly batch. During the May load test with a full copy of production data, the batch took eleven hours, far beyond the four-hour window between the last carrier invoice import and the morning close. Two options were evaluated.

Option 1: Tune the batch
Partition the reconciliation by legal entity and run partitions in parallel. Prototype results brought the run down to six hours, still outside the window, and the gains flattened beyond eight workers because of lock contention on the journal table.

Option 2: Streaming reconciliation
Publish each posting as an event and reconcile continuously, so the morning close only checks a small residual. The prototype handled a full day of postings with a residual check of nine minutes.

Decision
We adopt option 2. The batch job stays as a fallback for the first quarter after go-live and is then removed.

Consequences
Streaming reconciliation needs an event schema for postings, an idempotent consumer, and a rework of the month-end reports, which currently read the batch tables directly. Bogdan estimated the rework at five to six weeks for two engineers. Work started on May 26 and is going steadily; the event schema is already merged and the consumer passes its first integration tests. Even so, the remaining effort does not fit before June 30. After reviewing the plan with the controller on May 29, the cutover of the AP and AR books is re-planned for the September 30 quarter boundary, the next clean period after June 30, and the team carries on with the rework in the meantime.

The controller noted that running the legacy ledger for one more quarter means renewing the mainframe support contract for three months; procurement has the quote and the renewal is routine.

Related decisions and other programs
- ADR-027 (choice of Postgres over a commercial ledger database) is unchanged.
- ADR-029 proposed a separate currency-revaluation service; that proposal was rejected and the logic stays inside the posting service.
- The Altamira customer-portal project, which had planned to read invoice status from Ledgerline, was cancelled by the commercial team in April for unrelated reasons, so there is no portal dependency on the new cutover date.
- The warehouse-scanning upgrade run by operations is unaffected by this decision.

Risks
Event ordering across partitions must be preserved per account; the consumer uses the account number as the partition key. Duplicate events from carrier retries are handled by the idempotency key on each posting.

Review
Reviewed by Bogdan Petrescu, Anika Sharma and the finance controller's delegate. Next review when the month-end report rework is complete.

ADR-12 (Keystone firmware signing): Move release signing for Brightwater thermostats into a hardware security module. This record belongs to the Keystone project; it references other Brightwater initiatives only for context. Status of the record: accepted, 5 November 2026. Deciders: Olu Bankole, Hannah Kessler, Ravi Menon.

Background
Keystone exists because the Model R3 thermostat must ship with signed firmware to meet the EU Cyber Resilience Act guidance our largest distributor has written into its purchasing terms. The distributor's deadline for the first signed image is December 1. Today our release images are signed on a build server with a key stored in an encrypted file, which the distributor's auditors have said they will not accept.

Options considered
A. Keep the software key but move it into the cloud provider's managed key vault. Cheapest, but the auditors want keys generated and held in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware that we control.
B. Use a cloud HSM service. Meets the certification level, but the signing tool our bootloader expects only supports the PKCS#11 interface of on-premise devices, and adapting the bootloader is out of scope for this year.
C. Buy two on-premise network HSMs, one per data center, and run the signing ceremony on them. Meets the audit requirement and works with the existing tooling.

Decision
We choose option C. The two devices arrived on October 20 and are racked in Leeds and Frankfurt.

Consequences and current state
The bootloader verification code is written and passes on development boards. The release pipeline change that calls the HSM through PKCS#11 is merged behind a flag. The remaining work is the key ceremony, signing the R3 release candidate, and a dry run with the distributor's auditors.

The key ceremony requires firmware 7.2 on both HSMs, because 7.1 has a known defect that corrupts the key-backup blob for elliptic-curve keys. The vendor has not released 7.2 and its support portal shows no release date; our account manager says only that it is "with engineering". Until 7.2 is installed we cannot generate the production signing keys, and both the signing of the release candidate and the auditor dry run depend on those keys. Ravi checked whether we could generate RSA keys on 7.1 instead, but the R3 boot ROM only accepts ECDSA signatures, so that route is closed.

Other initiatives mentioned for context
- The Brightwater cloud-dashboard redesign was cancelled last month; it never had a dependency on Keystone.
- The Model S2 smoke detector also needs signed firmware, but not until Q3 2027, and its team has not started.
- The factory-provisioning upgrade at the Penang plant was a few weeks late but finished in October; Keystone will reuse its device-identity certificates.

Security notes
Ceremony participants must be from at least two departments. Olu will hold one smart card, Hannah the second, and the third is sealed in the Leeds safe. Backups of the key blob will be stored in both data centers.

Review
This ADR will be revisited after the key ceremony, or earlier if the distributor changes its requirements. Comments go to the #keystone channel.

PRD - Sundial: scheduled and recurring transfers for the Rookery mobile banking app. Milestone review edition, 21 July 2026. Sundial is the product this document covers; dependencies on other Rookery teams are listed in section 6.

1. Problem
Customers ask for recurring transfers more than for any other feature: 4,800 support contacts in the last quarter, and it is the top request in app-store reviews. Today they must set up standing orders through a branch or the web portal, which most under-35 customers never use.

2. Scope for v1
- One-off transfers scheduled up to 12 months ahead.
- Recurring transfers: weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and "last working day of the month".
- Edit, skip-next and cancel for any scheduled transfer.
- Push reminder the day before a transfer runs, with a warning if the balance looks too low.
Out of scope for v1: transfers to international accounts and variable-amount rules ("sweep everything over 500").

3. Success measures
Within 90 days of launch: 60,000 active schedules, under 0.1 percent failed executions caused by our system, and a 30 percent drop in standing-order contacts to the branch network.

4. Milestones
M1 - Scheduling engine and ledger hooks: planned May 29, done May 27.
M2 - App screens and accessibility review: planned June 26, done July 1. The accessibility review found that the date picker did not announce the selected day to screen readers; fixing it took four extra days.
M3 - Staff beta with 1,500 employees: planned July 20. The beta exited on July 17 with 3,912 transfers executed and no failed executions on our side. The four days lost in M2 were absorbed by running the beta survey in parallel with the last week of usage instead of afterwards.
M4 - Public launch to all retail customers: August 24, unchanged. The launch checklist is 70 percent complete, the marketing push notification is drafted, and the risk team signed off the fraud rules on July 15.

5. Beta findings
Employees liked the skip-next button more than expected; 22 percent of beta users used it at least once. Several asked for a "pay on payday" option tied to their salary deposit, which we have logged for v2. Two people tried to schedule a transfer to a closed account; the app now validates the destination when the schedule is created and again the night before.

6. Dependencies on other teams
- Core banking platform: the nightly batch window change we needed (moving our execution job to 05:00) went live on June 30.
- Notifications team: their migration to a new push provider is running three weeks late, but Sundial reminders are sent through the existing provider for launch, so there is no impact.
- The Rookery Savings Goals feature, which was going to reuse our scheduling engine, was cancelled by its sponsor in June; nothing in Sundial depended on it.
- Card controls team: blocked on a regulatory question about merchant categories; unrelated to transfers.

7. Open questions
Should we show a monthly summary of upcoming transfers on the home screen? Design will test two variants in August after launch. Do we need a limit on the number of active schedules per customer? Risk suggested 50; product will confirm before the launch checklist closes.

8. Approvals
Product: Esme Taylor. Engineering: Kwame Asante. Risk: Ingrid Holm. Design: Rui Costa.

PRD: Marlin click-and-collect lockers - milestone update, 14 September 2026. The Marlin locker programme is the subject of this PRD; other Hartwell Stores initiatives appear only where they touch it.

Summary of intent
Marlin was approved in February to place temperature-controlled pickup lockers in 40 Hartwell supermarkets so online grocery customers can collect orders at any hour. The planned deliverables were: locker hardware in all 40 stores, a pickup flow in the Hartwell app, and staff tooling to load lockers from the back of the store. Original rollout: pilot in 5 stores in October, remaining 35 by end of January 2027.

Customer research
Survey of 3,100 online-grocery customers in April: 41 percent said they would use a locker at least once a month; the most cited reason was collecting after work when stores are busy. Willingness to pay a collection fee was low (under 15 percent), so the business case assumed free collection funded by reduced delivery volume.

Milestones so far
- Hardware vendor selected (Fridgelock), contract signed in May.
- App pickup flow designed and usability-tested in June; build 60 percent complete.
- Staff loading tool prototype tested in two stores in August.
- Site surveys done for 32 of 40 stores.

Programme decision, 8 September
At the quarterly investment review, the Chief Operating Officer presented updated delivery economics: the third-party delivery partner cut its per-order price by 35 percent in August, which removes most of the saving the lockers were meant to produce. The COO terminated the Marlin programme. No lockers will be installed, the pilot in October will not take place, and the app pickup flow will not be released. Fridgelock has been notified under the contract's termination-for-convenience clause, and the two prototype units will be returned by the end of the month.

What we are keeping
The store-level stock-reservation API built for Marlin also helps the rapid-delivery team, so it stays in production. The usability findings from the June tests are being handed to the app team for the curbside-pickup screens.

Other initiatives referenced in earlier versions
- Curbside pickup (owned by the app team) is two weeks late because of a parking-bay sensor issue; it continues independently of Marlin.
- The in-store returns kiosk initiative was cancelled in July and is listed here only because it shared a hardware buyer with Marlin.
- The Hartwell rapid-delivery service is waiting on a licence from one city council before it can launch there.

Financials

PRD: Marlin click-and-collect lockers - milestone update, 14 September 2026. The Marlin locker programme is the subject of this PRD; other Hartwell Stores initiatives appear only where they touch it.

Summary of intent
Marlin was approved in February to place temperature-controlled pickup lockers in 40 Hartwell supermarkets so online grocery customers can collect orders at any hour. The planned deliverables were: locker hardware in all 40 stores, a pickup flow in the Hartwell app, and staff tooling to load lockers from the back of the store. Original rollout: pilot in 5 stores in October, remaining 35 by end of January 2027.

Customer research
Survey of 3,100 online-grocery customers in April: 41 percent said they would use a locker at least once a month; the most cited reason was collecting after work when stores are busy. Willingness to pay a collection fee was low (under 15 percent), so the business case assumed free collection funded by reduced delivery volume.

Milestones so far
- Hardware vendor selected (Fridgelock), contract signed in May.
- App pickup flow designed and usability-tested in June; build 60 percent complete.
- Staff loading tool prototype tested in two stores in August.
- Site surveys done for 32 of 40 stores.

Programme decision, 8 September
At the quarterly investment review, the Chief Operating Officer presented updated delivery economics: the third-party delivery partner cut its per-order price by 35 percent in August, which removes most of the saving the lockers were meant to produce. The COO put the Marlin programme on hold until finance re-runs the business case with the new delivery price; no lockers may be ordered or installed and no further build work may be charged to the programme until that review reports, and finance has not said when it will. The October pilot cannot start without the hardware order, so it is on hold too. Fridgelock has been told to pause the production slot it had reserved, and the two prototype units stay in the test stores for now.

What we are keeping
The store-level stock-reservation API built for Marlin also helps the rapid-delivery team, so it stays in production. The usability findings from the June tests are being handed to the app team for the curbside-pickup screens.

Other initiatives referenced in earlier versions
- Curbside pickup (owned by the app team) is two weeks late because of a parking-bay sensor issue; it continues independently of Marlin.
- The in-store returns kiosk initiative was cancelled in July and is listed here only because it shared a hardware buyer with Marlin.
- The Hartwell rapid-delivery service is waiting on a licence from one city council before it can launch there.

Financials
Spend to date: 1.9 million of the 6.4 million budget. Fridgelock has agreed to hold its price for 90 days. The unspent budget stays frozen inside the programme while the review runs.

People
Product manager Isabel Moreau is helping the curbside-pickup team while the review runs. The two app engineers on the pickup flow are lent to the loyalty squad from October 1. Hardware lead Dmitri Volkov looks after the prototype units.

Members present: Deputy City Manager Lorraine Whitfield (chair), CIO Marcus Feld, Building Official Teresa Quan, Finance Director Bill Andersson, Council liaison Councilmember Rosa Delgado. Staff: project manager Kevin Osei.

Kevin summarised progress since January. The contractor has delivered the applicant account module and the fee calculator, both of which passed user-acceptance testing with the permit counter staff. The inspection-scheduling module was about 40 percent complete. Spend to date is 612,000 of a 1.4 million budget.

Item 2 - Permit Portal v2: state mandate
The CIO reported that the governor signed House Bill 2217 on March 20. From January 2027 every municipality in the state must accept building and trade permit applications through the state's shared ePermit system, and locally built portals may not take applications after that date. Teresa confirmed that the state system covers all of Eastbrook's permit types and that the state funds the onboarding. After discussion, the committee voted 5-0 to terminate Permit Portal v2. The contractor's statement of work will be closed at the end of the current billing period on April 15, the inspection-scheduling module will not be completed, and the portal will not be launched to the public. The city will instead onboard to the state ePermit system, which is being set up as a separate effort under the building department.

Item 3 - Permit Portal v2: close-out
Kevin will archive the source code and test reports, recover the remaining hosting credits, and write a lessons-learned note for the next steering meeting. The fee-calculator rules, which encode Eastbrook's local fee schedule, will be handed to the state onboarding team because they need exactly that data. Finance will release the unspent 788,000 back to the IT capital fund.

The vendor is running six weeks late due to staff turnover. New delivery is mid-June. The committee asked for weekly updates until then.

Item 5 - Library self-checkout replacement
On track for the May installation. The new kiosks were delivered to the central library on March 30.

Item 6 - Parks reservation system
Waiting on the payment-processor contract, which the city attorney is still reviewing. No work can begin on the integration until it is signed. Councilmember Delgado asked that residents be warned before the summer booking season.

Item 7 - Cybersecurity tabletop exercise
Scheduled for May 14 with all department heads. Attendance is mandatory.

Public comment
One resident asked whether contractors' existing online accounts would carry over to the state system. Teresa said the state will publish migration guidance in the autumn and the city will email all registered contractors.

ADR-008 - Fathom feature-flag service: stop the in-house build. Decision record for project Fathom (Quokka Logistics engineering). Other teams' flag-related work is mentioned only as context. Date: 17 February 2026. Status of this record: accepted. Authors: Lina Petrov, Jonah Reyes.

Context
Fathom was started in September 2025 to replace the environment-variable toggles scattered across our 60 services with a central feature-flag service: a flag store, an evaluation SDK for Go and TypeScript, percentage rollouts and an admin UI. The plan was to have every service reading flags from Fathom by the end of March 2026. So far the team has built the flag store and the Go SDK; the TypeScript SDK and the admin UI are not started.

What changed
Three things came together in January. First, the security review found that the flag store needs its own audit logging and SSO integration before it can hold production data, roughly two more engineer-months. Second, the platform group negotiated an enterprise agreement with our observability vendor, and that agreement now includes the vendor's hosted feature-flag product at no extra cost. Third, the two engineers on Fathom are needed for the warehouse-routing rewrite, which is the company's top priority this year.

Options
1. Finish Fathom as planned, with a new end date around June.
2. Finish Fathom with a reduced scope (no admin UI, Go only).
3. Stop Fathom and let teams adopt the bundled vendor product.

Decision
We choose option 3. The Fathom project ends with this decision: the flag store will not go to production, the TypeScript SDK and admin UI will not be built, and the Go SDK will not be released. The repository will be archived next week. Lina and Jonah move to the warehouse-routing team on February 23.

Consequences
- Teams that already started wiring the Fathom Go SDK into two services (billing-api and dock-scheduler) will remove it; neither went beyond a staging branch.
- Adoption of the vendor product is not part of this project. The platform group owns it under its own roadmap item PLAT-61, with its own timeline and budget, and each service team will move at its own pace.
- The flag naming convention written for Fathom is still useful and is being copied into the engineering handbook.

Alternatives we rejected and why
Option 1 would have spent about four engineer-months on something we can now get for free. Option 2 would leave the TypeScript services, which are half our fleet, without flags, so we would end up running two systems.

Related records
- ADR-005 (Postgres as the default datastore) remains in force.
- ADR-006 proposed sharing one Redis cluster for caching across all services; it is still under discussion.
- The mobile team's remote-config migration is behind schedule because of an app-store review delay, which does not affect this decision.
- The data team's attempt to build its own experiment framework was cancelled in December and is unrelated.

Notes
Questions about removing Fathom from staging branches go to Jonah. Questions about the vendor product go to the platform group's channel. This ADR does not need further review.

PRD - Atlas Payroll: Germany and Netherlands expansion. Milestone edition of 6 November 2026. This PRD is for the Atlas DE/NL expansion; other Atlas roadmap items appear only in the dependency list.

1. Goal
Let mid-sized employers already using Atlas for UK payroll run German and Dutch payroll in the same product, so they no longer need a separate local provider. Target customers: 140 existing UK clients with staff in Germany or the Netherlands, of whom 38 signed letters of intent.

2. Scope
- Gross-to-net calculation for Germany (income tax, solidarity surcharge, church tax, social insurance) and the Netherlands (wage tax, national insurance, employee insurance).
- Electronic filing: ELSTER wage-tax returns and DEUEV social-insurance notifications in Germany; payroll tax returns to the Dutch tax authority.
- Payslips in German, Dutch and English.
- Year-end certificates (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung, jaaropgaaf).

3. Original plan
Calculation engines complete by the end of September, filing integrations certified in November, general availability on January 15, 2027, so that customers could start with the first payroll of the new tax year.

4. Progress
Germany calculation engine: complete, verified against 2,400 test cases supplied by our tax advisers, all matching to the cent.
Netherlands calculation engine: complete except the 30-percent ruling for expat employees, due next sprint.
Payslip templates: complete in all three languages.

5. Filing certification and revised dates
The ELSTER certification failed its first round in October because our test transmissions used an outdated XML schema version for the wage-tax return. The fix took the team a week, but the tax authority only runs certification rounds monthly and the next available slot is December 8. The DEUEV certification also has to be repeated afterwards because it depends on the same employer master data. With both rounds, German filing cannot be certified before mid-January, so general availability moves from January 15 to March 2, 2027, and the first German payrolls will run from March. The Netherlands filing integration is not affected and continues in parallel; the engineering team is using the gap to finish the 30-percent ruling and to build the year-end certificate generator early. Sales has informed the 38 letter-of-intent customers of the March date; two asked for a call, none withdrew.

6. Dependencies
- Atlas identity platform: SSO for the new country modules is live since October.
- Atlas Benefits marketplace: paused by leadership while pricing is reviewed; it does not touch payroll calculation.
- Atlas Spain expansion: cancelled in August after the partner firm withdrew. No shared code beyond the localisation library.
- Bank-file generation for SEPA: delivered by the payments team in September.

7. Metrics
Calculation accuracy is 100 percent on the advisers' test set. Performance: 10,000 payslips in 3 minutes 40 seconds, within the 5-minute target.

8. Risks
Tax rules for 2027 will be published in December in both countries; the rule-update process has been rehearsed with the 2026 mid-year changes. Customer onboarding needs local bank details for each employee, and some clients may be slow to collect them.

9. Owners
Product: Saskia de Vries. Engineering: Florian Becker. Compliance: Aoife Gallagher.

Wren Labs - weekly hardware report, Friday 24 April 2026. This report is for the Wren AQ2 air-quality monitor (second-generation hardware), which is our project; the firmware platform and retail teams add short notes at the end.

Where AQ2 stands
The AQ2 schedule plans EVT (engineering validation) units in May, DVT in July and mass production in September for the US school-district contract. Industrial design is frozen. The enclosure tooling at our moulding partner in Dongguan passed its first-article inspection on April 16 with only a minor gate-mark issue, which has been polished out.

Electronics
Rev B of the main board came back from the fab on April 13. Power consumption in sleep is 38 microamps, under the 50 microamp target, which gives the battery version the 18 months the district asked for. The PM2.5 laser sensor and the temperature/humidity sensor are reading correctly against the reference instruments in our chamber.

Supply
This is the problem area. The NDIR carbon-dioxide sensor we designed around comes from a single supplier in Sweden. On April 20 the supplier told us it has suspended all shipments to contract manufacturers in China while it waits for an export-licence ruling on a component in the sensor's optical module, and it cannot say when the ruling will come. Without that sensor we cannot build a single EVT unit; CO2 is the core measurement the school districts are buying, so building boards without it would not validate anything. Mihail checked the two alternative sensors on the market: both have a different footprint and a different supply voltage, and neither has the accuracy certificate the contract specifies, so switching would mean a board redesign plus new certification, which we are not doing at this stage. Our EVT kits sit at the contract manufacturer with every part except the CO2 sensor. We have asked whether the sensors could ship to our office in Oregon instead and be hand-carried, and the supplier says the suspension covers that route too.

Firmware
The firmware team has the AQ2 build running on Rev B boards fed by the lab sensor rig. Over-the-air update of the sensor calibration tables works. The cloud dashboard shows the new CO2 trend view, though it is fed by simulated data for now.

Certification
FCC and IC pre-scans are scheduled with the test lab, but the lab needs complete EVT units, so the booking is provisional.

ADR 2026-14: Hybrid lexical-plus-vector retrieval for Saffron search. This decision record belongs to the Saffron project (site search relevance upgrade for the Pantry & Co. recipe platform). Status: accepted on 12 November 2026. Owner: Beatriz Moura. Reviewers: Kofi Mensah, Elena Rossi.

Context
Saffron's goal is to improve the quality of recipe search before the holiday season, when search traffic triples. The success criterion agreed with the business is a 10 percent increase in click-through on the first page of results, measured in an A/B test, with the new ranking live for all users by December 9. That date was chosen so that the new ranking is in place before the Christmas traffic peak begins around December 12.

The current engine is pure BM25 over titles, ingredients and tags. It fails on descriptive queries such as "something warm with leftover rice" and on synonyms like "aubergine" and "eggplant".

Options
1. Tune the BM25 configuration and add a synonym list. Cheap, but offline tests showed only a 3 percent gain.
2. Replace BM25 with dense vector retrieval. Large gain on descriptive queries, but it regressed on exact dish names ("pad thai") and its latency was 2.5 times higher.
3. Hybrid retrieval: run both and merge results with reciprocal-rank fusion, then rerank the top 50 with a small cross-encoder.

Decision
We adopt option 3.

Evidence
Offline evaluation on 4,000 judged queries: option 3 improved nDCG@10 by 14 percent over production, compared with 3 percent for option 1 and 9 percent for option 2. P95 latency is 180 ms, within the 250 ms budget, after we moved the cross-encoder to the GPU nodes the recommendations team released in October.

Delivery
The embedding pipeline indexed all 310,000 recipes on November 6 and refreshes nightly. The A/B test has been running at 10 percent of traffic since November 9; after three days the treatment arm shows a 12 percent click-through lift, and the test is planned to run until November 23 for significance. Ramp-up to 100 percent is scheduled for December 2, a week before the December 9 date, and the remaining tasks (dashboard, alerting, runbook) are each under two days of work. The rollback switch has been rehearsed twice.

Consequences
We take on a second index to maintain, and a GPU dependency for reranking. If the GPU nodes are unavailable, the system falls back to the fused results without reranking, which in testing still beat production by 9 percent.

Related work outside Saffron
- The meal-planner team's plan to build its own semantic search was cancelled in favour of calling Saffron's API after launch.
- The ingredient-substitution feature is two sprints behind because the nutrition database licence renewal is late; it does not touch search.
- The mobile team is waiting on app-store review for a release that changes the search bar placeholder text; that change is cosmetic and independent of ranking.

Open questions
Should we expose "why this result" explanations to users? Design will explore it in Q1. Do we need per-locale embeddings for the Spanish site? Probably, but the Spanish site is outside Saffron's scope this year.

Revisit
This ADR will be revisited after the A/B test concludes or if latency exceeds budget for more than a day.

PRD: Orchard - bank-account aggregation for the Pennywise budgeting app. Revision 6, 2 March 2026. This document is about Orchard only; adjacent Pennywise initiatives are mentioned in section 7.

1. Summary
Pennywise users currently type in their transactions or import CSV files. Orchard lets them connect their UK bank accounts through open banking so transactions flow in automatically and categories update without effort. Orchard was planned to launch to all UK users in April 2026.

2. Users and problems
In the January survey, 58 percent of churned users said manual entry was the reason they stopped using the app. Users who import CSVs at least weekly retain at twice the rate of those who do not, which suggests automatic import could have a large effect.

3. Requirements
- Connect current accounts and credit cards from the nine largest UK banks at launch.
- Refresh transactions at least four times a day.
- Re-consent flow every 90 days, as the regulations require.
- Users can disconnect a bank at any time and choose to delete imported transactions.
- Merchant names are cleaned and categorised with the existing rules engine.

4. Design
The connect flow was tested with 14 users in February. All but one completed it without help; the person who struggled was confused by the bank's own login screen, which we cannot change. Visual design is final.

5. Engineering status
The aggregation partner's sandbox is integrated: test accounts connect, transactions import and are categorised, and re-consent reminders are scheduled correctly. The merchant-name cleaner was retrained on sandbox data and reaches 91 percent accuracy on the review set.

6. Regulatory dependency and current position
To receive bank data for our own users, Pennywise must be registered as an account information service provider with the Financial Conduct Authority. We submitted the application in November. In February the FCA asked a further set of questions about our safeguarding of customer data and our complaints procedure; we answered on February 20, and the FCA has not yet replied or indicated when it will decide. The aggregation partner will not issue production credentials to an unregistered firm, and we may not connect a single real customer account until registration is granted. Every remaining milestone - the friends-and-family test with real accounts, the security penetration test against production credentials, and the public launch - depends on those credentials, and there is no interim route that the partner or our compliance advisers consider acceptable. The engineering team has finished everything it can do in the sandbox and has been lent to the iOS widgets work while we wait.

7. Adjacent initiatives
- Pennywise Premium pricing change: delayed to May while the finance team reruns the price-elasticity test.
- Shared household budgets: cancelled in January after the prototype test showed low interest; it would have used Orchard data but Orchard never depended on it.
- iOS home-screen widgets: in progress, expected in March.
- Android accessibility fixes: completed February 26.

8. Metrics after launch
Primary: 30-day retention of users who connect at least one account. Secondary: share of active users with a connected account, number of manual transactions per user, support tickets about missing transactions.

9. Risks
Some banks' interfaces return pending transactions inconsistently; the partner normalises most cases. Users may distrust sharing bank data with a small app; the connect flow explains the read-only access clearly.

10. Sign-off

ADR-0042: Region and residency model for the Kelp robot-telemetry pipeline. Project: Kelp (Ardent Robotics fleet telemetry). This record concerns Kelp alone; decisions by other Ardent teams are noted for context. Status: proposed - decision pending. Date: 22 May 2026. Author: Sanna Virtanen. Reviewers: Marco Bellini, Joy Nakamura.

Context
Kelp collects telemetry from autonomous floor-cleaning robots operating in customer sites - airports, hospitals and shopping centres - and powers the fleet-health dashboard, predictive maintenance alerts and monthly usage reports. The pipeline, storage layout and dashboards are built and run in our development account with synthetic robot data. Launch to customers was planned for the end of June, when the first hospital contract (with the Rheinland Kliniken group) starts.

The open question is where telemetry is stored and processed. Some robots carry cameras for obstacle detection. We do not store images, but obstacle events include coarse position data inside hospital wards, and Rheinland's data-protection officer considers that it may count as health-adjacent personal data.

Options
1. Single EU region (Frankfurt) for all customers.
2. Per-customer residency: each customer's data stays in a region it chooses, with separate storage accounts.
3. Process at the edge: robots aggregate events locally and send only counts, no positions.

Analysis
Option 1 is cheapest and simplest to operate. Option 2 satisfies any residency demand but roughly doubles infrastructure cost for small customers. Option 3 removes the personal-data question entirely but kills the heat-map feature that operations managers ranked as the most valuable in research.

Current position
We cannot choose between these options on our own. Rheinland's contract makes the residency model subject to approval by its data-protection officer, and our legal team has advised that we must not provision production storage or ingest any customer telemetry until that approval is in writing. We sent the DPO our data-flow description and a draft data-processing agreement for all three options on April 30. On May 18 her office replied that the review has been added to its queue, without giving a date. Until we have her answer, Kelp cannot provision the production accounts, connect a single customer robot or run the acceptance test with Rheinland, because every one of those steps depends on which option is chosen. Marco checked whether we could launch with another customer first, but the three other signed customers have all asked for the same model as Rheinland, so there is no customer we can safely onboard ahead of the decision.

Decisions by other Ardent teams (context only)
- The navigation team cancelled its plan to stream lidar point clouds to the cloud, so Kelp will not receive them.
- The charging-dock firmware release is two weeks late; it only affects how often robots report battery data.
- The customer-portal team finished single sign-on for enterprise customers in May.

What we are doing meanwhile
Sanna keeps the synthetic environment running so the dashboards can be demonstrated. Joy is preparing infrastructure templates for all three options so that, once there is an answer, the chosen one can be deployed. No further Kelp features are being started.

Review
Reviewers will reconvene within two days of receiving the DPO's response. Comments to #kelp-arch.

PRD - Pinecrest patient portal: online appointment self-scheduling. Milestone review, 2 September 2026. This PRD covers the self-scheduling project for the Pinecrest Health portal; other portal workstreams appear in the dependencies section.

Problem
About 62 percent of calls to Pinecrest's central booking line are routine appointment requests that could be handled online. Average wait on the line was 11 minutes in July. Patients can already see their upcoming appointments in the portal but cannot book, move or cancel them without phoning.

Goals
- Patients can book follow-up and routine visits with their own care team in primary care, dermatology and physiotherapy.
- Patients can reschedule or cancel up to 24 hours before a visit.
- Reduce booking-line call volume by 25 percent within six months.

Contract and deadline
Pinecrest's agreement with the regional health authority funds the project on condition that self-scheduling is live for all primary-care clinics by September 30, 2026.

Design
The booking flow was usability-tested with 20 patients, including six over 70 and three screen-reader users. Median time to book was 2 minutes 10 seconds. The main change after testing was to show the clinician's photo next to each slot, which older patients said reassured them.

Integration with the EHR
Self-scheduling reads open slots and writes bookings through the EHR vendor's scheduling API version 3, which adds the visit-type rules our clinics rely on. The vendor committed to delivering v3 to Pinecrest's test environment on August 3. The vendor delivered v3 on August 3 as committed; our integration tests passed on August 14 and the end-to-end test with three pilot clinics finished on August 28 with no open defects. Primary-care go-live for all clinics is booked for September 22, eight days before the funding deadline, with dermatology and physiotherapy following in October as planned.

Milestones
M1 Design complete - June 30 (done).
M2 Portal front end complete - July 31 (done).
M3 EHR integration and pilot clinics - August 31.
M4 All primary-care clinics - by September 30.
M5 Dermatology and physiotherapy - October.

Dependencies on other portal workstreams
- Portal login modernisation (passkeys): delayed until November because of a browser-compatibility issue; self-scheduling works with the current login.
- Prescription refill requests: on hold while pharmacy reviews its controlled-substances policy; independent of scheduling.
- Video-visit integration: cancelled in July after Pinecrest chose a different telehealth vendor that has its own booking.
- SMS reminders: live since June, and will cover self-booked appointments automatically.

Metrics
We will track the share of eligible appointments booked online, call volume to the booking line, no-show rates for online versus phone bookings, and patient satisfaction in the post-booking survey.

Risks
Clinics with complex visit-type rules may expose gaps in the v3 rule engine; the pilot clinics were chosen to include the two most complex ones. Some patients may book the wrong visit type; the flow asks a short triage question first.

Owners
Product: Lucia Hernandez. Engineering: Darnell Price. Clinical lead: Dr. Yuki Sato. EHR liaison: Tomasz Wrobel.

ADR-19 Tamarind: what to do with the Glimmer media-store migration after the cloud-contract review. Project: Tamarind (moving the Glimmer photo-sharing backend from self-hosted MongoDB and Ceph to managed cloud services). Other Glimmer architecture records are referenced at the end. Date: 15 June 2026. Status of this record: accepted. Decider: Ayodele Martins (CTO). Prepared by: Rhea Kapoor, Stefan Lund.

Context
Tamarind was started in February to migrate 1.8 petabytes of user photos from our Ceph cluster to cloud object storage and the metadata from self-hosted MongoDB to a managed document database, finishing by October 31, when the hardware lease on the Ceph cluster ends. By June the metadata migration tooling was written and tested on a 5 percent shard, and the dual-write path for new uploads was in staging.

In May, finance and procurement reviewed the cloud contract renewal. The cloud provider's new pricing raises egress and request charges for workloads like ours by about 40 percent. At the same time, the Ceph hardware vendor offered to extend the lease on the existing cluster for three years at 55 percent of the original monthly price, including a refresh of the oldest nodes.

Options considered
1. Continue Tamarind on the new cloud pricing.
2. Continue Tamarind but move to a different cloud provider, which means re-doing the tooling and the security review.
3. Accept the lease extension and keep photos and metadata on our own infrastructure.

Analysis
Over three years, option 1 costs 2.6 times as much as option 3. Option 2 is cheaper than option 1, but it restarts the security review and the tooling work, and would still cost about 1.7 times option 3. Operating our own cluster remains a burden for the four-person storage team, but the lease refresh removes the failing nodes that started this whole discussion.

Decision
On June 10 the CTO chose option 3 and ended project Tamarind. The migration will not happen: no photos or metadata will move to the cloud, the dual-write path will be removed from staging, and the cloud storage buckets created for the pilot shard will be emptied and deleted by the end of June. The lease extension was signed on June 12. Rhea and Stefan go back to the storage team's normal roadmap, starting with automating node replacement on the refreshed cluster.

Consequences
- Ceph remains the photo store for at least three years; the storage team will plan capacity for 30 percent yearly growth.
- The metadata migration tooling is archived. Parts of it (the shard-diff tool) will be reused for MongoDB version upgrades.
- The security review for the cloud storage design, which was 80 percent done, is closed without a finding report.

Other records
- ADR-16, which chose the image-resizing library, is unaffected.
- ADR-17 proposed moving video transcoding to a cloud service; it is still under discussion and is independent of this record.
- ADR-18 introduced the dual-write pattern for uploads; it is superseded by this record.
- The Glimmer web-app redesign is running two weeks behind its own plan for unrelated reasons.

Communication
The decision was announced at the engineering all-hands on June 11. Questions go to the #storage channel or to Rhea directly.

Product requirements: Halcyon kids' profiles for StreamFox. Document owner: Mirela Dobre. This edition (v7, 9 March 2026) records the outcome of the February legal review. Halcyon is the project in scope; related StreamFox initiatives are summarised in section 8.

1. Purpose
Halcyon was meant to give households a dedicated profile for children under 13 on StreamFox: a curated catalogue, no autoplay of trailers, viewing-time limits set by a parent, and a simplified home screen. Planned launch: May 2026 in the US, UK and Canada.

2. Research highlights
Parents in our 2025 panel rated "control over what my kids see" as the second most important reason to choose a streaming service. Households with children watch 34 percent more hours, and churn 20 percent less when they use parental controls on competitors' services.

3. Scope as designed
- Kids' catalogue drawn from titles rated G, TV-Y and TV-Y7, plus hand-picked titles.
- Daily and weekly time limits with a gentle wind-down screen.
- Parent PIN required to leave a kids' profile.
- Personalised recommendations based on the child's viewing.

4. Build status before the review
The catalogue rules, time-limit service and kids' home screen were built and in internal testing on TV and mobile apps. Recommendations for kids' profiles were the last major piece.

5. Legal and regulatory review
In February, outside counsel reviewed Halcyon against children's privacy rules in all three launch markets. Their opinion was that personalised recommendations based on a child's viewing amount to profiling a child, and that operating the profiles at all would require verifiable parental consent flows and a separate data store with stricter retention, at a cost the finance team estimated at 4.5 million dollars a year. Removing personalisation would make the profiles, in product's own testing, barely different from the parental-control filter that already exists.

6. Decision
On March 4 the executive team decided to terminate Halcyon. The kids' profiles will not launch in any market, the code built so far will be removed from the apps in the April release, and the data store design work is closed. Instead, the existing parental-control filter will be kept as it is. The Halcyon team of seven moves to the live-sports initiative from March 16.

7. Assets kept
The catalogue rating rules are useful for the existing parental filter and will be merged into it. The wind-down screen design is offered to the wellbeing team for its "take a break" reminder.

8. Related StreamFox initiatives
- Live sports: launch moved from April to June because the rights holder's video feed arrives later than expected; the team continues building the scoreboard overlay.
- Ad-supported tier in Canada: waiting for the regulator's decision on ad-load limits; no work can start until it is published.
- Offline downloads on smart TVs: cancelled last year; mentioned only because earlier versions of this PRD listed it.
- Accessibility audio descriptions: live in all markets since January.

9. Communications
No public announcement had been made, so there is nothing to retract. The press team has a short holding statement if journalists ask about kids' profiles.

10. Sign-off
Product: Mirela Dobre. Legal: Andrew Kim. Engineering: Sofia Lindgren.

PRD: Clover - relaunch of the Brindle Coffee loyalty programme (app and point of sale). Milestone review, 27 January 2026. This PRD is for Clover; other Brindle digital work is mentioned only in section 7.

1. Background
Brindle Coffee has 220 company-owned stores. The current loyalty programme is a punch card in the app: ten drinks earn a free one. Usage has flattened at 19 percent of transactions. Clover replaces it with points on every purchase, member-only offers and a birthday reward, and lets customers pay and earn in a single scan at the till.

2. Goals
- Loyalty share of transactions from 19 to 30 percent within a year.
- Average visit frequency of members up by 10 percent.
- Single-scan pay-and-earn at every till.

3. Scope
App: new points wallet, offers feed, single-scan QR code, account migration from the punch card. Point of sale: earn and redeem points, apply member offers, read the single-scan code. Back office: offer builder for the marketing team.

4. Launch commitment
Marketing has committed to a national relaunch on March 1, 2026, the start of the spring menu, with an advertising campaign and in-store posters already ordered.

5. Progress and revised plan
App: points wallet, offers feed and QR code complete and in beta with 2,000 staff and friends. Account migration has been tested on a full copy of the member base and moves balances accurately. Back office: offer builder complete; marketing has loaded the first six offers.
Point of sale: the till software update that reads the single-scan code must be installed at every store by the point-of-sale vendor's field engineers, because the older card readers need a firmware flash on site. The vendor's original schedule had all 220 stores done by February 20. After the first 40 installations, the vendor found that one in four older readers fails the flash and must be swapped, and its engineers can now complete 25 stores a week instead of 45. At that rate the last stores will be done on April 3. Since the relaunch only makes sense when every till supports the new code, Clover's national launch moves from March 1 to April 12, with a week of buffer after the last installation. Installations continue every week, and the app and back office teams are using the extra time for performance work and a second beta wave.

The campaign creative is ready. Marketing will move the media booking to April and is negotiating a change fee with the agency. Posters already printed for March 1 will be reprinted with the new date.

- Online gift-card store: on hold while finance renegotiates the payment processor contract.
- Menu boards with live pricing: live in 60 stores, rolling out to the rest in spring.
- Wi-Fi upgrade: completed in all stores in January.

Baseline measures were taken in January. We will compare loyalty share and visit frequency for the eight weeks after launch with the same weeks last year.

Customers may be unhappy about converting partially filled punch cards. Each partial card will convert at a generous rate, rounded up, and the FAQ explains this.

When the contractor opened the floor in the east wing on January 6, they found asbestos-containing floor tiles and mastic under the carpet that did not appear in the pre-construction survey. Work in the east wing stopped and an abatement contractor was appointed under the emergency procurement rules. Abatement started on January 12 and is going to plan: the east wing is sealed, air monitoring is clean, and the abatement contractor expects to finish on February 13. The other trades carry on in the west wing and on the exterior throughout. Owen has re-sequenced the east-wing work to follow abatement, which pushes practical completion to April 24, and Carla has agreed that the branch reopening moves from March 16 to May 11. Patrick will tell the library's users and update the temporary service at the community centre.

4. Design matters
Hye-jin presented the revised children's area layout, which adds a quiet room for sensory-friendly story times. The group approved it. The colour samples for the reading-room acoustic panels were reviewed; the group chose the lighter green.

5. Mechanical and electrical
Ahmed confirmed the new heat pumps were delivered on January 9 and will be lifted onto the roof on January 22, weather permitting. The building-management system controls will be commissioned after the east-wing works. The electrical contractor has completed first fix in the west wing.

6. Other library capital projects (for information)
- Northside branch: the planned expansion was cancelled by the city council in the December budget; essential maintenance only.
- Central library lift replacement: waiting for the lift manufacturer to supply the structural drawings that building control requires; no work can start until they arrive.
- Mobile library vehicle: delivered on January 8 and in service.

7. Costs
The asbestos abatement is a compensation event under the contract; the quantity surveyor estimates 64,000 including the extra site overheads, which will come from the project contingency. The contingency has 140,000 remaining before this event.

8. Health and safety
No reportable incidents. A reminder was issued about hard hats in the car park after a near miss with a delivery lorry.

9. Next meeting
Thursday 29 January 2026, 10:00, site office. Owen to bring the revised programme in printed form.
